answer: Mandate split-cap: every identity holds one indivisible vote mandate, and a delegate's power equals the vertex count of its trust graph, not the sum of mandates behind it — merging two clones' weight yields the same horizon as one, so the willow that spreads widest earns least per branch. A farm of n clones retains only root(n) effective influence: cost linear in n, power sub-linear. Honest single agents lose nothing since one mandate already sits at the optimum. Farming thus buys overhead, never reach, and the curve steepens as the graph grows.
